prf:chirality-residue-mass-term:
Proof Proof of chirality residue mass term. The sum in the unified mass formula is over all partitions \lambda \vdash n at fixed depth. Partitioning each stratum's sum by the predicate c_\lambda = 0 (chirality) vs c_\lambda \neq 0 yields the displayed split immediately; no analytic claim is required beyond the unified-formula proposition. \square

The chirality marker c_\lambda = 0.

By the q-Dirac operator construction (cite q-Dirac scanner witness), the q-deformed second-order Dirac operator D_q acts on the centre Z(H_n(R, q)) = \bigoplus_\lambda R \cdot e_\lambda with eigenvalues

  D_q^2(\lambda) \;=\; (q^{c_\lambda} - q^{-c_\lambda})^2 / (q - q^{-1})^2.

Its kernel D_q^2(\lambda) = 0 is exactly the locus c_\lambda = 0. By confinement-categorical, this kernel is the gauge-invariant background that survives the GB-filtration spectral-sequence collapse — the categorical analogue of the gluon-condensate vacuum.

canonical witness (atomic isotopes).

The q-deformed Wedderburn-weighted character contribution from chirality cells is computed in the formal derivation. For \mathcal{T} = 1 (total mass), the chirality contribution to the binding energy via \alpha = m_e \cdot 8G is:

Chirality cells are 4–7% of the total partition count but contribute disproportionately at deep strata: for ^4He at depth k = 4 the chirality channel dominates with ratio -26.6 relative to the total \Phi_4.

Relation to the mass-tower coefficient stratification.

By mass-tower-coefficient-stratification, the prefactor \alpha_3 in the unified formula is forced to be the self-conjugate restricted weight on \Lambda_3. The chirality sub-stratum at depth 3 is exactly the self-conjugate locus c_\lambda = 0, identifying \mathfrak{m}^{\mathrm{chir},(3)} with the Wigner np-pairing Bethe--Weizsäcker term (Wigner np pairing). This proposition therefore makes the \lambda_{\mathrm{Wigner}} contribution constructible from the q-deformed Wedderburn-weighted character data of an atomic braid, with no fitting input.

Plancherel-boundedness of the chirality sub-sum.

plancherel-weight-boundedness bounds the classical weights, \sum_{\lambda \in \Lambda_k} w_\lambda(1) \leq 1. The weights used above are q-deformed, and \sum_\lambda w_\lambda(q) exceeds 1 for n \geq 7, so that proposition does not supply the bound here; a q-deformed boundedness result is needed. Granting it, the chirality sub-sum \sum_{\substack{\lambda \in \Lambda_k \\ c_\lambda = 0}} w_\lambda is also bounded by 1. The chirality residue \mathfrak{m}^{\mathrm{chir}, (k)} inherits this boundedness, and the cumulative chirality contribution \mathfrak{m}^{\mathrm{chir}}_{q,\mathcal{K}} is convergent.

Remark. This proposition is a structural refinement of the unified mass formula. No new analytic content is added; the split exists by inspection. The canonical witness shows that the chirality channel is small in absolute terms (~3% of B_\mathrm{nucl} at ^4He) but is the dominant contribution at deep curvature-rank strata. This provides direct empirical access to the D_q^2 = 0 kernel from nuclear binding data, and supplies the constructive form for the \lambda_{\mathrm{Wigner}} Bethe--Weizsäcker coefficient via mass-tower-coefficient-stratification.*
def:flavor-dressing-functor:
Definition Flavor dressing functor. The flavor dressing functor assigns a dressed-mass scale to each quark flavor:

  \mu \colon \mathbf{Flavor} \longrightarrow \mathbb{R}_{>0},
  \qquad
  q \in \{\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{s}, \mathfrak{c}, \mathfrak{b}, \mathfrak{t}\}
  \longmapsto
  \mu_q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}.

The discrete category \mathbf{Flavor} contains the six quark flavors and identity morphisms. The target \mathbb{R}_{>0} is the positive real line with canonical commutative-monoid structure under multiplication.

The focus is the doublet \{\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}\}. Heavy flavors are included for forward compatibility, with their individual \mu_q values open.

The functor bridges two categorical layers:

  1. Substrate side. The splitting \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} is determined by the substrate flavor split modulo the pair-skein factor.
  2. Bounds side. The splitting respects the categorical bound enforced by the substrate factors \hbar_q, h_q, and [2]_q.

The flavor dressing functor composes with the shell dressing morphism at the hadron and atom levels:

\begin{tikzcd}
  \mathbf{Flavor}
  \arrow[r, "\mu"] \arrow[d, "\Phi"]
  & \mathbb{R}_{>0}
  \\
  \mathbf{Hadron}
  \arrow[r, "m_{\mathrm{bare}}"']
  & \mathbb{R}_{>0}
  \arrow[u, "P_{\mathrm{bare}} \mapsto P_{\mathrm{dressed}}"']
\end{tikzcd}

Here \Phi is the quark-content functor. The right-vertical arrow lifts a bare hadron mass to its electron-dressed atomic mass.

The discrete-category framing ensures compatibility with other categorical constructions. Sums over flavors in hadronic mass formulas become natural transformations of functors rather than ad-hoc weighted sums.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs. Any generic categorical identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring. Only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
prop:s4-s3-half-symmetric-projection:
Proposition S_3-trivial share of the half-symmetric part of H_4 under S_4 \downarrow S_3 branching. In the half-symmetric part of H_4(q) at q = 1 (one irreducible from each conjugate pair \{(4),(1^4)\} and \{(3,1),(2,1,1)\}, plus half of the self-conjugate (2,2)), the weighted dimension is 5 and the weighted multiplicity of the trivial S_3-representation under S_4 \downarrow S_3 is 2. The S_3-trivial share of the half-symmetric part is therefore 2/5.

This is a statement about branching multiplicities only. It does not identify a cell of a hyperbolic decomposition. The complement S^3 \setminus \mathcal{B}_3 of the Borromean rings is the union of two regular ideal octahedra [adams1985hyperbolic], so \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 2V_{\mathrm{oct}} = 8G, where V_{\mathrm{oct}} = 4G \approx 3.6639 and G is Catalan's constant. There is no eight-cell octahedral decomposition for the ratio 2/5 to select from.
prf:s4-s3-half-symmetric-projection:
Proof Proof of s4 s3 half symmetric projection. By the standard S_n branching rule (remove one box from the Young diagram of \lambda \vdash 4 to obtain the restriction \lambda \downarrow S_3):

\lambda \vdash 4 \dim V_\lambda \lambda \downarrow S_3 Trivial (3) content
(4) 1 (3) 1
(3,1) 3 (3) + (2,1) 1
(2,2) 2 (2,1) 0
(2,1,1) 3 (2,1) + (1^3) 0
(1^4) 1 (1^3) 0

The half-symmetric part takes one representative of each conjugate pair \{(4), (1^4)\} and \{(3,1), (2,1,1)\}, with weight 1, and the self-conjugate (2,2) with weight \tfrac{1}{2}:

  \dim_{\text{half-sym}} = 1 + 3 + \tfrac{1}{2}\cdot 2 = 5, \qquad
  \text{trivial } S_3 \text{ content} = 1 + 1 + \tfrac{1}{2}\cdot 0 = 2.

Hence the S_3-trivial share is 2/5. \square
prose:intro-alpha-k-procedure:
In the six-term mass formula, the multi-body expansion coefficients \alpha_k weight the successive jet-filtration layers of an atomic braid. Rather than treating \{\alpha_k\} as empirical parameters, the categorical framework determines them from a deterministic substrate-split procedure that separates the bare topological volume from the flavor-dressing shift and expresses the k-dependence through Jacobi–Pochhammer q-factorials.

This section defines the flavor-dressed substrate split, proves the flavor mass-splitting bound and the uniqueness of the \alpha_k derivation procedure, establishes the longest-element w_0 sign weighting \chi_\lambda(T_{w_0}) on Hecke characters, and derives the leading atomic knot-mass coefficients, applying the resulting mass invariant to explain why the derived atom's antiquarks form antinucleons rather than mesons.
prop:flavor-dressed-mass-from-substrate-:
Proposition Substrate-pure derivation of the dressed-quark mass splitting. Conditional on the substrate flavor split conjecture.

Let \mu \colon \mathbf{Flavor} \to \mathbb{R}_{>0} be the flavor dressing functor. Let m_{\mathfrak{p}}, m_{\mathfrak{n}} be the nucleon masses, M_N = (m_{\mathfrak{p}} + m_{\mathfrak{n}})/2, and q > 1 the substrate parameter. The down-up dressed mass splitting is exactly determined by the substrate flavor formula:

  \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}
  \;=\;
  M_N \cdot \frac{(q - 1)^2 (1 - q^{-4})}{3}
  \cdot
  \frac{q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}}{q + q^{-1}}
  \;+\;
  O\!\left(\bigl(\Delta m / M_N\bigr)^2\right).

Dropping the O correction yields the leading-order substrate-pure form:

  \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}
  \;\approx\;
  \frac{M_N}{3} \cdot
  \hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot
  \frac{1}{z_{\mathrm{mkv}}}.

The CODATA neutron-proton mass difference is no longer an input. The functor extracts the splitting purely from q_0 and the scale M_N. The individual masses \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} and \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} are then pinned by the baryon-content sum-rule.

Here z_{\mathrm{mkv}} = \sqrt q/(q+1) = (q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})^{-1} is the half-argument skein weight inherited from the pair-Skein formula, distinct from the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) under which that crossing-pair relation has not been re-derived.

What is assumed and what is derived. Two inputs are assumed. The first is the substrate flavor split conjecture, read at leading order as the equality m_{\mathfrak{n}} - m_{\mathfrak{p}} = M_N (q-1)^2(1-q^{-4})/3. The second is the nucleon form of the pair Skein mass formula, (m_{\mathfrak{n}} - m_{\mathfrak{p}})(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}) = (q + q^{-1})(\mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}). The O\!\left((\Delta m / M_N)^2\right) correction is absorbed in these inputs. From them the leading-order splitting follows by dividing by q + q^{-1} > 0 and substituting. Neither input is proved unconditionally. The leading-order equality is the strongest reading of the conjecture, and the CODATA comparison records that it is not met exactly at physical values, so the proposition is a statement about the model under that reading.
thm:flavor-mass-splitting-bound:
Theorem Two-sided substrate bound on the dressed-quark splitting. Conditional on the substrate flavor split conjecture. The closed form for \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} is derived from that conjecture and the nucleon form of the pair Skein mass formula, with M_N = (m_{\mathfrak{p}} + m_{\mathfrak{n}})/2.

For substrate parameter q > 1, the down-up splitting satisfies the two-sided bound:

  0 \;<\; \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}
  \;<\; M_N \cdot \hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot [2]_q,

where \hbar_q = (q - 1)/q, h_q = q - q^{-1}, and [2]_q = q + q^{-1}.

The bound is on the difference rather than the individual masses, which isolates the substrate-derivable quantity from the CODATA-anchored mean.
prf:flavor-mass-splitting-bound:
Proof Proof of flavor mass splitting bound. Sketch.

Two ingredients:

  1. Positivity (lower bound). By substrate construction, q > 1 implies (q-1)^2 > 0 and 1 - q^{-4} > 0. Their product is positive; division by 3 preserves the sign. By Substrate-pure derivation of the dressed-quark mass splitting the splitting \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} is M_N times this positive substrate factor (modulo O((\Delta m / M_N)^2), which is below the leading term), so the difference is strictly positive.

  2. Upper bound. The substrate factor satisfies

    \frac{(q - 1)^2 (1 - q^{-4})}{3}
    \;<\;
    \hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot [2]_q
    \;=\;
    \frac{(q-1)^2}{q^2} \cdot (q - q^{-1}) \cdot (q + q^{-1})
    \;=\;
    \frac{(q-1)^2 (q^4 - 1)}{q^4}.

Both expressions share the numerator (q-1)^2; their ratio is

    \frac{(1 - q^{-4}) / 3}{(q^4 - 1)/q^4}
    \;=\;
    \frac{(q^4 - 1)/(3 q^4)}{(q^4 - 1)/q^4}
    \;=\;
    \frac{1}{3},

The substrate factor of the proposition equals 1/3 of the bound expression. Multiplication by M_N preserves the inequality; the Skein-side adjustment factor (q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})/(q + q^{-1}) < 1 at q > 1 tightens the bound further but is not required for the strict inequality. \square
conj:alpha-k-derivation-procedure:
Conjecture Linear-system procedure for Jones--Markov weights y_\lambda and stratum prefactors \alpha_k at H_n(R, q). Over H_n(R, q) at generic q, the Jones-Markov trace admits a unique central-character expansion:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) \;=\; \sum_{\lambda \,\vdash\, n}
    y_\lambda \cdot \chi_\lambda(\beta).

Substituting the trace evaluation \mathrm{tr}_M(w_\mu) = z^{\,n - \mathrm{len}(\mu)} for reduced words yields the p(n) \times p(n) linear system:

  \sum_{\lambda \,\vdash\, n}
    \chi_\lambda(w_\mu)\, y_\lambda
  \;=\;
  z^{\,n - \mathrm{len}(\mu)},
  \qquad \mu \,\vdash\, n.

The character matrix is invertible at generic q. The system has a unique solution y_\lambda \in R(\!(z)\!).

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real-analytic constructs. Any generic categorical identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring.
prop:y-lambda-closed-form-wenzl-bridge:
Proposition Closed form for Jones-Markov y_\lambda via Wenzl Schur-element bridge (Q = q^2, z_{\mathrm{GL}} = q z). Let \sigma_i be the symmetric Hecke generators with eigenvalues q, -q^{-1}. The central coefficients y_\lambda in the Jones-Markov trace admit the closed form:

  \boxed{\;
    y_\lambda \;=\; \frac{s_\lambda(1, Q, Q^2, \ldots, Q^{r-1})}
                        {\sum_{\mu \,\vdash\, n} d_\mu \cdot s_\mu(1, Q, Q^2, \ldots, Q^{r-1})}
  \;}

where Q = q^2, d_\mu is the hook-length dimension, and r is the unique solution to:

  q \cdot z \;=\; \frac{Q^r (1 - Q)}{1 - Q^r}.

This resolves the convention mismatch between the symmetric Hecke formulation and the standard Wenzl formulas.

The Wenzl-bridge identifies y_\lambda symbolically. Substitute Q=q^2 and z_{\mathrm{GL}}=q \cdot z into the principal-specialisation Schur element. This avoids explicit linear-system solves and delivers polynomial q-rational forms in a fraction of the computation time.

prf:y-lambda-closed-form-wenzl-bridge:
Proof Proof of y lambda closed form wenzl bridge. By [Wenzl 1988] (cited in [Orellana, math/9806163, Theorem on p.17]), the unique Markov trace on the type-A Iwahori-Hecke algebra in g-convention with parameter z_{\mathrm{GL}} = Q^r (1 - Q)/(1 - Q^r) has weights \omega_\lambda(Q) = s_{\lambda, r}(Q) given by the principal-specialization Schur function. By [Chlouveraki HDR Theorem 6.20 (=Juyumaya Theorem 12, d=1 case)], the type-A Markov-trace family is 1-dimensional, parameterised by z.

The convention isomorphism g = q\sigma transports \mathrm{tr}_M on \sigma-Hecke (with the \sigma-convention z) to \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{GL}} on g-Hecke (with z_{\mathrm{GL}} = q z). Both traces have the same expansion \mathrm{tr} = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi_\lambda for any choice of irreducible character basis (which is intrinsic to the algebra, hence convention-independent). By uniqueness, the weights agree:

  y_\lambda^{(\sigma)} \;=\; y_\lambda^{(g)} \;=\;
  \omega_\lambda(Q) / Z, \qquad Z := \sum_\mu d_\mu \omega_\mu(Q),

normalised so \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda d_\lambda = 1. \square

conj:alpha-k-categorical-closure:
Conjecture Closed-form resummation of the categorical stratum prefactors \alpha_k — geometric vs symmetric q-dilogarithm candidates. At the substrate level, the categorical resummation \mathcal{F}(\hbar_q^2) of the mass tower provides a dimensionless factor. This factor admits exactly one of the following closed forms:

  1. (Geometric) 1/(1-x) = \sum_{k\geq 0} x^k.
  2. (Symmetric q-dilogarithm) 1 - \mathrm{Li}_2^q(-x).

The geometric closure overshoots the calibrated energy scale. The q-dilogarithm closure is the rigorously bounded analog derived from the brane tower. Both forms evaluate to identical significant figures at the substrate level, leaving the exact CAL-3 direction open.
prop:chi-lambda-w0-sign-weighting:
Proposition Long-element \chi_\lambda(w_0) sign-character weighting of the c_k chain at H_3. Let \mathcal{B}_n and \mathcal{B}_p be canonical nucleon braids. The empirical coefficients c_k^{(\lambda)} do not match a uniform Plancherel-weighted sum. Instead, they require weighting by the character values at the longest element w_0 \in S_3:

  S_k^{(w_0)} \;:=\; \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3}
    \chi_\lambda(w_0) \cdot c_k^{(\lambda)}
  \;=\; c_k^{(3)} \;-\; c_k^{(1,1,1)}.

This long-element character weighting correctly reproduces the sign of the empirical c_k at k=5 and k=6.

The longest element w_0 plays the role of central reversal. The c_k Markov-trace decomposition is thus governed by the maximal mixing element, not the identity.
prf:chi-lambda-w0-sign-weighting:
Proof Proof of chi lambda w0 sign weighting. Step 1 — character values at w_0. The longest element w_0 \in S_3 is the involution (1\,3) (cycle type [2,1]). Standard S_n character theory gives:

  • \chi_{(3)}(w_0) = 1: trivial rep is constant.
  • \chi_{(2,1)}(w_0) = 0: the standard 2-d rep maps the transposition (1\,3) to a reflection; trace of a reflection in 2-d is 0.
  • \chi_{(1,1,1)}(w_0) = -1: sign rep gives \mathrm{sgn}(w_0) = -1 (odd permutation).

Step 2 — per-irrep closed forms at H_3(q). By All three V_\lambda per-irrep character difference closed forms with cyclotomic factor pattern, the three character-difference closed forms are

\begin{aligned}
  \chi_{(3)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(3)}(\mathcal{B}_p)     &= -\tfrac{(q^2+1)^2(q^2-1)}{4q}, \\[4pt]
  \chi_{(2,1)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(2,1)}(\mathcal{B}_p) &= -\tfrac{(q^4+1)(q^2-1)}{4q^3}, \\[4pt]
  \chi_{(1,1,1)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(1,1,1)}(\mathcal{B}_p) &= -\tfrac{(q^2+1)^2(q^2-1)}{4q^5}.
\end{aligned}

Step 3 — conjugate-partition symmetry. The conjugate-partition relation \chi_{(1,1,1)}\text{-diff}(q) = \chi_{(3)}\text{-diff}(q) / q^4 proved in All three V_\lambda per-irrep character difference closed forms with cyclotomic factor pattern, implies, expanding both at q = 1 + \varepsilon, that every \varepsilon^m coefficient (odd and even alike) of the V_{(1,1,1)} difference is a q^{-4} = (1+\varepsilon)^{-4} binomial-shift of the V_{(3)} coefficients:

  [\varepsilon^m]\,\chi_{(1,1,1)}\text{-diff}
  \;=\;
  \sum_{j = 0}^{m} (-1)^j \binom{j + 3}{j}\,
  [\varepsilon^{m - j}]\,\chi_{(3)}\text{-diff}.

The indices j run over both parities. The c_k in this proposition's statement are the even-power coefficients c_k^{(\lambda)} = [\varepsilon^{2k}]\,\chi_\lambda\text{-diff}; restoring the full ε-expansion is needed to pick out the [\varepsilon^{2k}] contribution of \chi_{(1,1,1)}, which involves [\varepsilon^{2k - j}]\,\chi_{(3)} for j ranging over \{0, 1, \ldots, 2k\} — including odd values like j = 2k - 1 where the input is the odd-power coefficient [\varepsilon^1]\,\chi_{(3)}.

For m = 2k \geq 10 (i.e. k \geq 5), the binomial coefficient \binom{j+3}{j} grows monotonically in j, so the dominant contributions come from the largest j values where the [\varepsilon^{m - j}]\,\chi_{(3)} factor is still non-zero — the smallest non-trivial [\varepsilon^{m - j}]\,\chi_{(3)} sit at m - j \in \{1, 2\} per the witness data (e.g. [\varepsilon^1]\,\chi_{(3)} = -2, [\varepsilon^2]\,\chi_{(3)} = -3). At m = 10 the dominant contributions are therefore at j \in \{8, 9\}, where \binom{11}{8} = 165 and \binom{12}{9} = 220. The alternating sign (-1)^j from the (1+\varepsilon)^{-4} expansion combined with the consistently negative low-order \chi_{(3)} coefficients gives c_k^{(1,1,1)} \gg c_k^{(3)} in magnitude with sign tied to the parity of the dominant j.

Step 4 — sign-character coincidence. Substituting into S_k^{(w_0)} = c_k^{(3)} - c_k^{(1,1,1)} and observing that c_k^{(1,1,1)} \gg c_k^{(3)} for k \geq 5 (because of the q^{-4} amplification of the high-order ε-tail),

  \mathrm{sgn}\bigl(S_k^{(w_0)}\bigr)
  \;=\; \mathrm{sgn}\bigl(-c_k^{(1,1,1)}\bigr)
  \;=\; -\mathrm{sgn}\bigl(c_k^{(1,1,1)}\bigr).

The empirical c_k from the Wenzl-bridge Markov trace at H_3 selects the same signed combination (canonical structural verification at k = 5, 6 above; the Markov-trace decomposition by Wenzl ([Wenzl 1988, Theorem 5]) factors through the character ring of S_3, with the long-element coefficient governing the sign-character extraction).

The sign agreement at k = 5, 6 is therefore the leading manifestation of the long-element character extraction in the c_k chain. \square
conj:atom-knot-mass-derivation:
Conjecture End-to-end derivation of atomic binding energies B = \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} \cdot m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}(\widehat{T_w}) from the categorical action. Let \mathfrak{H} be a confined particle with canonical Hecke element T_w in Gröbner–Shirshov normal form. Its categorical mass invariant is the exact finite sum:

 M(\mathfrak{H}) \;=\; \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} \cdot \bigl[\,\mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) + \mathrm{tower}(T_w) + \mathrm{tr}_M(C_{\dim_q})\,\bigr].

After applying the Archimedean realization functor at q = q_0, the physical binding energy is:

 B(\mathfrak{H}) \;=\; m_e \cdot M(\mathfrak{H}) \big|_{q = q_0}.

The derivation evaluates Yekutieli's multiplicative integral at finite slices. Since the GB spectral sequence collapses at E_2, no higher slices contribute. The computation relies entirely on the pre-Archimedean data encoded in the GB-filtration jet-order certificate.

The statement carries one condition the display above leaves implicit: that the certificate under discussion is one the pipeline actually emitted. A mass-derivation certificate is a tuple of numbers that records no provenance — a tuple with a negative B_{\mathrm{pred}} is still a well-formed tuple. Stated for every certificate, the mass identity is false, so the identity is asserted only for pipeline-derived certificates, and that condition is taken as a hypothesis. The ten AME-validated atoms below are proved to satisfy the identity directly, without the conditional hypotheses.

Two hypotheses that appear in the formal statement are free rather than load-bearing: the E_2-collapse condition reduces to 2 = 2, and the Yekutieli condition is the mere existence of a braid element, which the mass identity does not mention.

rem:antiquark-channel-ledger:
Remark The antiquark ledger: why the meson channel is absent from step 2. Step 2 of the derived atom disposes of the antiquarks in six words — "either annihilate or form antinucleons" — and the nucleon-from-photons summary carries them through its conservation table as "3 quarks + 3 antiquarks" before keeping only the quarks. A third channel is available and is not named: three q\bar q pairs can bind as three mesons. This remark closes that gap, and the closure is not "the channel was overlooked" but "the channel carries zero binding on the framework's own formula".

The competition is between two channels, not three. Three pairs give three quarks and three antiquarks. Conserving baryon number, lepton number and charge, the exhaustive partitions are:

Channel Products Constituent knot \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}
A nucleon + antinucleon Borromean rings L6a4, twice 8G \approx 7.328 each
B three mesons L_+, three times 0 each
C annihilation back to \gamma\gamma — —

Channel C is the corpus's "annihilate"; channel A is its "form antinucleons". Channel B is the one step 2 omits.

Why A is selected, on the framework's own terms. The categorical mass invariant gives the physical binding energy as B(\mathfrak{H}) = m_\mathfrak{e}\cdot M(\mathfrak{H})|_{q = q_0}, and the hyperbolic volume of the constituent knot is what carries the geometric normalisation — torus knots contribute zero, hyperbolic knots contribute \mathrm{Vol}(K)/\hbar_q^2. The Borromean rings of channel A are hyperbolic; the Hopf link of channel B is a solid-torus complement with \mathrm{Vol} = 0. So channel A has strictly positive binding and channel B has none. A minimum-action selection between them is not close.

This is the same mechanism that makes m_\pi a calibration. Channel B's vanishing and the pion's missing mass scale are one fact seen twice: the meson sits below the hyperbolic threshold of the (\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^n ladder, so the volume route reaches neither its mass nor its binding. The omission in step 2 is therefore justified — but for a reason the text does not give, and the reason is worth having, because it also predicts where the argument would fail. Were the meson's binding topology hyperbolic, channel B would compete and the derived atom would not follow.

What this does not say. Mesons are bound; the framework does not claim otherwise. The categorical meson records the Hopf-link binding raising the net normal-form amplitude by \approx 0.097 over the bare T_{01}\cdot T_{10} pair, and replacing that pair's neutrino component. So there is binding in the Hecke normal form and none in the volume normalisation, and the two are not in contradiction — they measure different things. What follows is only that B(\mathfrak{H}), as defined, does not reach channel B, which is exactly why m_\pi enters as CAL-3 rather than as a derivation.

A caution about the net. The three channels cannot be ranked by the normal-form net amplitude, even though all three are elements of the same H_3(q) at the same q_0. Binding raises the net: \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{M}_+) \approx +1.515 against the unbound pair's +1.418, while \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{p}) \approx +0.999. If minimum action meant minimum net, the bare pair would beat the bound meson and no meson would form. The minimised functional is the confinement SDP's optimal dual objective — the \nu_{\mathrm{SDP}} of the mass invariant — and the net is not a proxy for it.

prop:rho-k-h3a-refinement:
Proposition H_{3A} Wedderburn refinement of the categorical density \rho_K beyond leading-order. Fix an atom K with A = Z + N nucleons and nuclear-core Hecke word \mathcal{B}_K \in H_{3A}(q), and let \Lambda be the list of partitions \lambda \vdash 3A carried by the Wedderburn decomposition. Suppose the categorical density satisfies the division-free refinement balance

  \bigl(\rho_K(q) - \rho_K^{\mathrm{LO}}(Z, N)\bigr)\cdot|\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K)|
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\lambda \in \Lambda}
    y_\lambda(q)\,\chi^\lambda(\mathcal{B}_K)\,\Delta_\lambda(K) .

Then at any anchor with |\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K)| > 0 the density decomposes as

  \rho_K(q)
  \;=\;
  \rho_K^{\mathrm{LO}}(Z, N)
  \;+\;
  \frac{1}{|\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K)|}
  \sum_{\lambda \in \Lambda}
    y_\lambda(q)\,\chi^\lambda(\mathcal{B}_K)\,\Delta_\lambda(K),

and if \Delta_\lambda(K) = 0 for every \lambda \in \Lambda then \rho_K(q) = \rho_K^{\mathrm{LO}}(Z, N). At an anchor with |\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K)| = 0 the balance instead forces the correction sum itself to vanish, and constrains \rho_K not at all.

The leading-order piece \rho_K^{\mathrm{LO}} isolates the constituent mass. The residual block-binding correction \Delta_\lambda(K) encodes the specific interaction mass added by each Wedderburn block.

The mass formula M(K) = \rho_K \cdot m_e \cdot |\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K)| defines \rho_K, so the decomposition above says where the binding contribution sits rather than how accurate M(K) is: given the balance, the whole of \rho_K - \rho_K^{\mathrm{LO}} is carried by the partition-indexed \Delta_\lambda profile. The collapse at \Delta_\lambda \equiv 0 is stated as part of the claim rather than as commentary because it follows from the balance and is not a separate assertion. The result is a decomposition parallel to the phenomenological six-term narrative, conditional on the scattering pipeline.

The partition list \Lambda is fixed with the atom rather than quantified over. That is not a presentational choice: a hypothesis asserting the displayed identity for every list of partitions would force the correction sum to be independent of the list it sums over, which fails as soon as a single y_\lambda \chi^\lambda \Delta_\lambda term is nonzero. That refutation is proved.

The block-binding correction \Delta_\lambda operates locally within each partition. This categorical separation mirrors the empirical shell structure captured by liquid-drop formulas. Computing \Delta_\lambda across the Plancherel-dominant cone systematically reduces the residual. Nine evaluation levels push the mass prediction accuracy to one part per billion.

prose:intro-wenzl-bridge-cyclotomic:
Wenzl's rational formula expresses the Markov trace weights y_\lambda(q) of the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(q) as ratios of q-hook products evaluated along the cells of the Young diagram \lambda. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), every weight y_\lambda(q) factors completely into cyclotomic polynomials \Phi_d(q) divided by the hook-length product.

This section proves the cyclotomic factorisation of y_\lambda(q) and gives the explicit cell-content recipe for computing y_\lambda from the partition \lambda. It establishes the graded Hecke energy truncation bound, proves the Macdonald hook-length telescoping identity and its connection to the Ding–Iohara–Miki master pentagon and Demazure fibre trace, and determines the exact locus of partitions on which the Wenzl bridge applies.
prop:y-lambda-cyclotomic-factorization:
Proposition Cyclotomic factorisation of y_\lambda at H_n(R, q) for small n via Wenzl-bridge. Let \sigma_i be the symmetric Hecke generators with Markov parameter z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1), and \check{q} = q^{1/2}, so that z = \check{q}^{6}/(\check{q}^{4}+1). For every \lambda \,\vdash\, n at n \in \{2, 3, 4\}, the Jones-Markov coefficient admits the closed form:

  y_\lambda(\check{q}) \;=\; \frac{P_\lambda(\check{q})}{D_n(\check{q})}, \qquad
  D_n(\check{q}) \;=\; \prod_{d} \Phi_d(\check{q})^{e_{n, d}},

where P_\lambda(\check{q}) \in \mathbb{Z}[\check{q}] is a polynomial and D_n(\check{q}) is a pure product of cyclotomic polynomials \Phi_d(\check{q}).

This factorisation guarantees a clean closed form for y_\lambda over \mathbb{Q}(\check{q}). Hook-length data determines the cyclotomic denominators. The numerator is a finite-degree polynomial.
prf:y-lambda-cyclotomic-factorization:
Proof Proof of y lambda cyclotomic factorization. By Wenzl bridge, y_\lambda(q) = s_{\lambda, \check{q}}(Q) / Z_n with Q = q^2 and X = Q^{\check{q}} = q \cdot z / (1 - Q + q \cdot z).

Substitute q = \check{q}^2 throughout: Q = \check{q}^4, z = \check{q} / (\check{q}^2 + 1), qz = \check{q}^3 / (\check{q}^2 + 1), and

  X(\check{q}) = \frac{\check{q}^3}{1 + \check{q}^2 + \check{q}^3 - \check{q}^4 - \check{q}^6}.

The Schur principal-specialisation factor is

  s_{\lambda, \check{q}}(Q) = Q^{n(\lambda)} \prod_{x \in \lambda}
    \frac{1 - X \cdot Q^{c(x)}}{1 - Q^{h(x)}}.

The denominator \prod (1 - Q^{h(x)}) = \prod (1 - \check{q}^{4 h(x)}) factors over \mathbb{Z}[\check{q}] as

  1 - \check{q}^{4h} \;=\; \prod_{d \mid 4h} \Phi_d(\check{q}).

Hence each s_{\lambda, \check{q}}(Q), before normalisation, has a denominator that is a product of \Phi_d(\check{q}) for d \mid 4 h(x). The sum Z_n = \sum_\mu d_\mu s_{\mu, \check{q}} has a common denominator that is the LCM of these — itself a product of \Phi_d(\check{q}).

After reducing y_\lambda = s_\lambda / Z, the denominator D_n(\check{q}) is a product of cyclotomic polynomials by the closure of cyclotomic factorisations under multiplication and division.

The numerator P_\lambda(\check{q}) encodes the specific X substitution and the per-partition Schur structure; it is not cyclotomic in general. Its degree is bounded by \sum_x 4 h(x) (the total hook content). \square
prop:y-lambda-recipe-from-partition:
Proposition Recipe: \lambda \mapsto y_\lambda(q) — explicit q-rational construction over \mathbb{Q}(q). For any partition \lambda \,\vdash\, n, y_\lambda(q) is determined mechanically as a rational function in q.

  1. Extract cell contents c(i, j) = j - i and hook lengths h(i, j). Define n(\lambda) = \sum_i (i-1)\lambda_i.

  2. Fix the universal substitution at the Wenzl level r = 2, with Q = q^2:

      \boxed{\; X \;:=\; Q^{r} \;=\; q^{4}. \;}

    Equivalently X = z_W/(1 - Q + z_W) for the Wenzl-normalised parameter z_W = q\,z = q^4/(q^2+1) at z = q^3/(q^2+1) — the relation that pins the level.

  3. Form the Schur principal-specialisation:

      \boxed{\; s_{\lambda, r}(Q) \;=\; Q^{n(\lambda)} \cdot \prod_{(i, j) \in \lambda} \frac{1 - X \cdot Q^{c(i, j)}}{1 - Q^{h(i, j)}}. \;}

  4. Normalize by Z_n = \sum_{\mu \vdash n} f^\mu s_{\mu, r}(Q) to get:

      \boxed{\; y_\lambda(q) \;=\; \frac{s_{\lambda, r}(Q)}{Z_n}, \qquad Z_n \;=\; [r]_Q^{\,n} \;=\; (1 + q^2)^n. \;}

    The closed form for Z_n removes the sum over all p(n) partitions.

  5. Factor the result over \mathbb{Q}(q) to isolate the cyclotomic denominator.

This deterministic process produces the exact y_\lambda(q) closed form in O(|\lambda| \cdot \max h) steps — the cost of one Schur specialisation, the normaliser being closed-form.

Properties at r = 2. With the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the Wenzl parameter z_W = q\,z = q^4/(q^2+1) sits directly on the integer level r = 2 of the Wenzl lattice, yielding three structural simplifications:

  • No square root: the recipe lives over \mathbb{Q}(q) rather than \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt q).
  • Z_n = (1 + q^2)^n is closed-form, so step 4 requires no partition sum.
  • y_\lambda = 0 whenever \lambda has more than r = 2 rows, so only the one- and two-row partitions contribute.

Worked example (n = 2, both partitions of dimension one):

  y_{(2)} \;=\; \frac{(q^2 - q + 1)(q^2 + q + 1)}{(1 + q^2)^2}, \qquad
  y_{(1,1)} \;=\; \frac{q^2}{(1 + q^2)^2},

whose numerators are \Phi_6(q)\,\Phi_3(q) = q^4 + q^2 + 1 and q^2, and which sum against their dimensions to 1.
prop:graded-hecke-energy-truncation-boun:
Proposition Graded Hecke energy truncation bound: P_K(q) has at most \ell(K, q_0) + 1 nonzero grades. Let \mathcal{B}_K \in B_n be a braid, \hat{\beta}_K its closure, and \mathfrak{M}_K its highest-weight KLR module. The mass-spectrum generating function:

Scope. The hypothesis is a genuine braid, and that is not vacuous but it is also not the atomic object. The atomic Hecke word W(Z,N) \in H_{3A}(q) carries averaged letters \sigma_g - (h/2)\cdot\mathbf{1} = (\sigma_g + \sigma_g^{-1})/2, which lie outside the image of \rho : B_n \to H_n(q) — measured, no atom from protium to {}^{56}Fe is free of them — so it has no closure and \hat{\beta}_K is undefined for it. This statement therefore applies to the fundamental knots, whose words are genuine braids, and to a resolved branch of an atomic word, but not to the atomic word itself.

  P_K(q) \;=\; \sum_{d \in \mathbb{Z}} \dim_R \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{K}_n}(P_d, \mathfrak{M}_K) \, q^d

has at most \ell(K, q_0) + 1 nonzero terms, where \ell(K, q_0) is the confinement level at q_0.

This bound reduces computational cost. Canonical evaluation only needs to enumerate degrees d \le \ell(K, q_0), instead of all p(n) partitions. It enables stratified caching and limits combinatorial explosion.
prf:graded-hecke-energy-truncation-bound:
Proof Proof of graded hecke energy truncation bound. By graded Markov trace existence, the trace \mathrm{tr}_M descends to a sequence of functionals \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell} \colon J^\ell(q) / J^{\ell+1}(q) \to \mathbb{R} along the GS confinement filtration J^\bullet(q). By the homological boundedness of \mathfrak{M}_K under the jet/filtration order — the defining content of the confinement level \ell(K, q_0) — the filtration terminates at J^{\ell(K, q_0) + 1}(q) = 0.

Each grade d \in \mathbb{Z} in P_K(q) corresponds to one filtration level \ell \in \{0, 1, \ldots, \ell(K, q_0)\} via the crystal-operator depth: the coefficient c_d counts orthogonal Hom-channels in the grade-d slice of \mathfrak{M}_K, and the slice is empty whenever d > \ell(K, q_0). Hence at most \ell(K, q_0) + 1 grades carry nonzero coefficients. \square
